description: Every diagnostic code the vectors use. A tolerable code is one a lenient decoder may accept with a warning (a strict decoder rejects it); the others are errors in both modes, or information only. Implementations map these ids to their own names; a new code is added here first. The separate `refusals` list names the reasons an encoder or builder refuses data; it is its own namespace, with no tolerable flag, and a refusal id never appears in a diagnostic.

codes.meaning: The TNC2 header is not SOURCE>DEST[,PATH]:.
An address is empty, too long, or has characters that cannot appear in one.
The destination address is empty (UAP 5.2).
The digipeater path has an empty entry (UAP 5.6).
More than one path entry is marked used with *; only the last used one should be (UAP 5.30).
The AX.25 frame is not a UI frame with PID 0xF0, or is too short (APRS12c ch. 3).
An AX.25 address is padded with NUL rather than spaces (UAP 5.29).
An AX.25 address has lower-case letters; any other character that is not an upper-case letter or digit makes it invalid-address.
The AX.25 frame has more than 8 digipeater addresses.
The information field ends with CR or LF (APRS12c ch. 5, UAP 5.13).
Text that is not valid UTF-8 (UAP 5.16).
Text holds a byte below 0x20 or the byte 0x7F (a TAB, or a CR or LF inside the text, included); one per text, which is kept as sent (APRS12c gives text as printable characters).
The information field is shorter than its format requires.
The first byte is not a data type identifier (APRS12c ch. 20).
A reserved data type identifier with no defined format (APRS12c ch. 5).
A format the spec marks obsolete or not recommended, e.g. raw NMEA, raw weather, or the Rev 0 Mic-E data type identifiers 0x1C and 0x1D.
A value in a well-formed field is out of range and was dropped.
A timestamp is malformed or out of range (APRS12c ch. 6, UAP 5.8).
The position is missing or starts with something that cannot begin one.
The latitude is malformed (APRS12c ch. 6, UAP 5.7).
The longitude is malformed (APRS12c ch. 6, UAP 5.7).
A lower-case hemisphere letter (UAP 5.9).
The symbol table identifier is not /, \, 0-9 or A-Z.
The symbol code is not printable ASCII.
A compressed position is malformed (APRS12c ch. 9).
A !DAO! adds precision to an ambiguous position, which contradicts it.
A data extension (PHG, RNG, DFS) appears later in the comment (UAP 5.15).
The object name is empty or not printable ASCII.
The object name is not padded to 9 characters.
An object report has no timestamp (APRS12c ch. 11).
The item name is not 3-9 printable characters followed by ! or _.
A weather report lacks a mandatory field (APRS12c ch. 12).
Text after the weather data; weather reports have no comment (UAP 2.7.1, ch. 5.33).
Positionless or raw weather data that could not be decoded.
The destination address is not a valid Mic-E encoding (APRS12c ch. 10).
The Mic-E information field is malformed (APRS12c ch. 10).
Kenwood TM-D710 0xFF padding was removed from Mic-E status text, after the destination and the nine fixed bytes decoded (UAP 5.10).
A Mic-E report without a device type prefix (UAP 5.4).
A message is malformed (APRS12c ch. 14).
The addressee is not padded to 9 characters.
An ack or rej carries a message ID of its own (UAP 5.32).
A telemetry metadata message (PARM/UNIT/EQNS/BITS) is malformed (APRS12c ch. 13).
A directed query is malformed (APRS12c ch. 15, UAP 5.18).
A telemetry report is malformed (APRS12c ch. 13).
A status report is malformed (APRS12c ch. 16).
A Maidenhead locator is malformed.
The text after $ is not an NMEA 0183 sentence: not printable ASCII, no valid address field, or a reserved character in a field.
An NMEA sentence's checksum does not match, so the sentence is corrupt and is not decoded.
A third-party header is malformed, or (strict) its inner header has a defect a lenient decoder tolerates (APRS12c ch. 17).
A general query is malformed, or its footprint is out of range (APRS12c ch. 15).
A station capabilities report is malformed (APRS12c ch. 15).
A user-defined packet is shorter than its 3-byte header (APRS12c ch. 19).
An Agrelo DF report is not exactly %, a bearing of 000 to 360, / and a quality digit.
A grid-locator status report lacks the mandatory space before its text (UAP 5.17).
A compressed position's type byte sets its unused high bits (APRS12c ch. 9).
A timestamped position report whose timestamp is missing or not timestamp-shaped (UAP 5.8).
A ! position found after other text (obsolete TNC beacon rule).
A weather field is one character shorter or longer than its fixed width (UAP 5.31).
Wind sent as c/s fields in a position weather report instead of the DDD/SSS extension, or after a compressed position whose cs bytes carry no wind.
An uncompressed wind extension after a compressed weather position (UAP 5.33).
A Mic-E altitude after other status text instead of first (APRS12c ch. 10).
Message, bulletin or telemetry metadata text contains a { that does not start a valid message ID, including the reply-ack form on a bulletin or metadata (APRS12c ch. 14).
A message addressee contains a space or : (APRS12c ch. 14).
A bulletin addressee has a group name after a letter, e.g. BLNCNET; group bulletins use a digit (APRS12c ch. 14).

A < station capabilities packet holds free text rather than TOKEN / TOKEN=VALUE items: a token that is empty or holds a space or a control character, or a value that holds a control character (APRS12c ch. 15).

The packet needs more than the implementation's fixed capacity holds (an information field, path entries, capabilities, extra weather fields); only an implementation with such a capacity gives it, as a header error or with the data unrecognized, and never reads the packet differently instead.

refusals.meaning: A header address (source, destination, path entry, or a third-party one) is not 1-9 letters, digits or `-` in TNC2 text.
An AX.25 frame cannot carry the header: a call over 6 characters or in lower case, an SSID over 15 or written with a leading zero or as -0, more than 8 path entries.
A TNC2 line cannot carry the packet: its information field is not UTF-8 text.
A third-party packet's inner header cannot be written as received: a bad inner address, used markers out of order, or a tolerated defect that is part of its data.

A message, bulletin, NWS bulletin, telemetry metadata or directed query addressee is empty, over 9 characters, holds a space or `:`, or is not the form its report needs (`NWS-`/`NWS_`, a group bulletin's digit).
An object or item name is the wrong length or holds a character a name cannot.
A message ID is empty, over 5 characters or not letters and digits, or an ack or reject carries the wrong kind of ID.
Text starts or ends with a space that would be read back as padding (an object name, a capability value).

Free text or a list is longer than its field allows (message text over 67 characters, a project title over 23, more than 13 names, more than 5 analog values), or the information field as written is over 256 bytes (APRS12c ch. 3).
Text in a fixed-form field is not that form: a locator, a bit sense, telemetry bits, signpost text, a capability token, a weather extra field, too few telemetry values.

Free text holds a character its field cannot carry: a control character (a byte below 0x20, a line break included, or 0x7F), a `{` in message-like text, or a character outside printable ASCII where only that is allowed.

Free text would read back as a structured element (an altitude, a `!DAO!`, telemetry, a frequency, PHG/RNG/DFS, a timestamp or locator, a Mic-E device suffix, a weather field), and no clean form avoids it.
A value is NaN or infinite.
A number is outside what its field holds, after rounding (latitude, speed, gust, snowfall, range, footprint, bearing, telemetry sequence, PHG and DFS digits, an SSID).
A value inside the range that no form reads back as: a course of 0 in Mic-E or compressed bytes, a humidity of 0, Mic-E telemetry 255, `T#MIC` with an empty first channel, a frequency between bands.
A builder input was given in two units (Celsius and Fahrenheit, feet and metres, mm and inches).
A timestamp has a field out of range, or is a format the report does not take (a status not DHM, MDHM outside a positionless weather report).

The data lacks something its report or another field needs: an object's timestamp, a capability, a compressed course without its speed, wind direction without speed, a tone without a frequency, a GGA type without an altitude.
The symbol table or code is not a valid symbol.
The symbol disagrees with the data: weather without `_`, `_` without weather, an area without `\l`, a DF bearing without `/\`, a signpost without `\m`.
Two things want the one data extension or the cs bytes: course/speed with PHG, a DF bearing with RNG, a compressed course with a range, wind with a range, a weather report's wind with a course.

The report has no place for a field, or it contradicts another: a compressed report with PHG, area or ambiguity, Mic-E with weather or an area, weather with a comment, telemetry or frequency, a locator status with a timestamp, a `!DAO!` on an ambiguous position.
An enumerated value outside its set: a Mic-E message with mixed bits or custom over 6, a Mic-E type code, a beam heading or power code, a query type, a DAO datum, a compression type, a tone type.
An NMEA sentence is malformed, its checksum does not match, or a field given beside it disagrees with it.
The call has nothing it can write: undecoded data, or Mic-E through a call that cannot return the destination.
Fallback: the library's own read-back check found the bytes decode to different data and no rule above names why.
